card: Adds `#include <util/check.h>` and removes `<cassert>` across unit tests and benchmarks via a scripted diff, followed by an include sorting pass. This addresses confusion over whether assertions can be disabled under `NDEBUG` and improves compatibility with automated Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) analysis. The author notes that building without assertions in `util/check.h` currently causes compile errors. The change is restricted to test and benchmark files.
evidence: Author description: 'sometimes confusion arises, when it is unclear whether NDEBUG can disable the assertions, or whether to use assert or Assert. Avoid that confusion in test code with a scripted replacement to add the util/check.h include. The changes here will also make it easier to run IWYU.'
Commit fab3f83f9a message: 'The project has a compile error when compiled without assertions in util/check.h. Thus, util/check.h should be included for all assertions.'
problem: Test and benchmark files frequently rely on transitive includes or standard `<cassert>`, leading to confusion over whether assertions can be compiled out by `NDEBUG` and complicating automated Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) passes.

risk.why: Only touches include headers in test and benchmark files; a failure would manifest as a compile failure in tests.

scope_notes: Mechanically generated scripted-diff affecting 51 test and benchmark files.
summary: Runs a scripted diff across unit tests, IPC tests, Qt tests, and benchmarks to add `#include <util/check.h>` and remove `#include <cassert>` wherever assertions appear. A second scripted commit re-sorts modified include blocks using clang-format.
